newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila property firms unfazed by glut scare.
newsitem.headline: Manila property firms unfazed by glut scare.

text.p: Three Philippine property companies are forging ahead with projects despite the scare of a possible crash in the local real estate market, company officials said on Friday.

"No project will be slowed down. Projects in the pipeline will proceed as scheduled," Andrew Tan, chairman and president of Megaworld Properties & Holdings Inc, told reporters after its stockholders' meeting.
The company and its subsidiary, Empire East Land Holdings Inc, are completing seven housing projects this year, after selling seven other projects in 1996.
Tan said the company would be raising 2.5 billion pesos ($95 million) through a stock rights offer to finance new projects beyond 1997.
As a show of confidence, Tan said he and his associates, who hold more than 70 percent of Megaworld, would fully subscribe to the stock rights.
"We like to send a very strong signal to the market that we are very confident about the long-term prospect of the real estate industry in the Philippines," Tan said.
Megaworld and Empire have been battered severely in the local bourse since the start of April as rumours of a cash crunch spooked investors.
The selldown triggered industry-wide selling, but eventually spread to the whole market as investors started to draw parallels between the Philippines and the recent Thailand property crash.

Earlier on Friday, Filinvest Land Inc (FLI) president Mercedes Gotianun said FLI would launch in the second half of the year its Filinvest Sky City, a 677-hectare golf and luxury residential community in eastern Manila.
New residential villages around Manila and regional centres such as the central Cebu and southern Davao cities would also be launched by FLI.

"FLI looks to the future with renewed optimism. As the Philippine economy gets stronger, rising per capita income will increase the demand for housing in all market segments," Gotianun said in her report to stockholders.

In a separate statement, Philippine Estates Corp said it was set to launch 12 diversified real estate projects such as high-rise apartments, colonies with individual houses, industrial estates, and a leisure community, all in Manila and its immediate environs.
